r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Independently reproduced ALL required evidence: (1) py -m pytest tests/unit/physics/layer2/test_fp_representativeness.py -q -> 35 passed (matches handoff); (2) grep -nE 'FP1|FP2|FP3|session_type' src/physics/layer2/fp_representativeness.py -> empty, exit 1 (matches); (3) git status --short data/ -> clean; (4) py -m src.utils.simplification_limits --baseline --paths <both files> -> PASS (2 files checked). CENTRAL CHECK (critic F3/F4 calendar-in-disguise guard) hand-verified by recomputing observation_weight's sigmoid arithmetic outside the test suite: TEST 1 (within-session) -- track_evolution_score(35) with no session_max is IDENTICAL for both observations by construction (35/(35+40)=0.46667 for each, confirmed both by the test's own equality assertion and my independent recompute); the weight gap (push=0.9974 vs long_run=0.6136 under DEFAULT_WEIGHT_PARAMS) is therefore driven entirely by fuel_proximity/compound_softness/run_purpose_score, which do differ (0.9975/1.0/1.0 vs 0.0183/0.3/0.2) -- a real, non-tautological discrimination. Companion test (w_track_evolution=0) recomputed too: zeroing the term still leaves push=0.9959 > long_run=0.499, confirming the gap survives independent of any track-evolution term. TEST 2 (cross-session) -- recomputed track_evolution_score(8)=0.16667 vs track_evolution_score(70)=0.63636: the LATER/long-run observation has the track-evolution ADVANTAGE, exactly as the test's own line-361 assertion states and as I independently confirmed. Despite that, recomputing the full weight gives w(earlier_push)=0.9965 > w(later_long_run)=0.6482 -- the ranking is REVERSED relative to track_evolution_score alone. This is the precise 'a track-evolution-only weighting would get this backwards' property the handoff/critic demanded, and it is asserted programmatically (not just claimed in prose) via the test's own pre-check assertion before the weight comparison. Structural corroboration: w_track_evolution=1.0 is deliberately the smallest of the four feature coefficients (fuel=2.5, run_purpose=2.5, compound=1.5, track_evolution=1.0) per the module's own DEFAULT_WEIGHT_PARAMS docstring -- consistent with, not merely coincidental to, the emergence property. VERDICT: the emergence tests are genuine, non-trivial discriminators, not weak/tautological checks -- they would fail under a track-evolution-only (calendar-in-disguise) weighting and pass only because the implementation is truly multi-feature. No BLOCK trigger present: no session-type string (verified), no binary-drop (observation_weight's logistic range is the open interval (0,1), TestNothingBinaryDropped exercises out/in/thin-long-run cases and all return positive bounded weights, no None path in source), no Q-session leakage (track_evolution_score signature is exactly {track_evolution, session_max_track_evolution}, both plain ints per TestLeakageGuard + manual read of fp_lap_latent.py confirms FpLapLatent.fuel_kg_est/compound/run_purpose are FP-observed/emergent fields, not Q-derived), no real-data fit (DEFAULT_WEIGHT_PARAMS is hand-set, module contains no fitting/optimization code path).
